messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Hi John — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the technical/contract asks you surfaced: 

1) Data residency requirement: ACME wants EU-customer data to remain in EU regions and US-customer data to remain in US regions.
2) Cross-region failover: acceptable if tenant data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and if failover only occurs for availability events (no long-term replication outside the primary region).
3) Backups & DR: ACME needs clarity on backup storage locations, retention windows, and the ability to disable cross-region backups for EU tenants.
4) Logging & PII: request for redaction options in application logs and control over retention for request/response logs that may contain PII.

Per our platform: we support region pinning per-tenant, can configure cross-region failover policies, and offer customer-controlled KMS keys for encryption. I attached a short one-pager on our region-pinning model (redwood-region-pinning.pdf) and a draft MAP for procurement (MAP-ACME-2891.xlsx).

Can you confirm the items above and let me know if you want us to propose a detailed MAP that includes RTO/RPO targets and a proposed acceptance test for a short POC?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Aditya — thanks for the summary. Confirming the high-level asks and adding clarifications from the security & legal side: 

- EU residency: EU customer data must be stored and processed in EU physical regions. Metadata that does not contain PII may be allowed outside EU, but request to identify what "metadata" fields are considered safe.
- Failover: short-term automatic failover is OK for availability events; long-term read replicas in a different region are not acceptable unless encrypted and explicitly enabled per-tenant.
- Backups: backups must be stored in the same region by default; cross-region replication must be opt-in on a per-tenant basis. Retention: default 30 days, with ability to extend.
- Logs: need options to suppress or redact request/response bodies from operational logs; audit logs for admin actions are fine with standard retention.

Please include specific language we can hand to procurement/security (bullet points) around data-at-rest encryption, KMS controls, and where backups are stored. Also send your SOC 2 report/attestation.

John Ellison
Head of Cloud Security
ACME Bank
john.ellison@acmebank.com

Hi John — adding some specifics from a product perspective to help your security/procurement team: 

- Region pinning model: we support tenant-level region pinning. For each tenant you can: designate a primary region, enforce strict regional-only storage (no background replication outside primary), or allow controlled failover with safeguards.
- Backups & DR: snapshots/backups are stored in the tenant's primary region by default. Cross-region replication is an explicit opt-in that can be disabled per-tenant. Backups are encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys (if requested).
- Failover behavior: automatic failover is available but by default runs in the same cloud region family (e.g., eu-west-1 AZ failover). Cross-region failover is available as a configured policy with documented failback and data synchronization steps.
- Logs & PII: we provide redaction hooks at the ingestion layer and configurable retention policies for request/response logs. Audit logs are retained per contract.

I've attached our SOC2 attestation and a short product FAQ on region pinning. Happy to have a 30-minute follow-up with your security team to walk through the controls and the MAP.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Looping in next steps from a sales/ops perspective — we should convert this into a tight MAP and propose acceptance criteria for the POC. Suggested items to include: 

- Scope: single tenant in EU with primary region eu-west-1, single tenant in US with primary us-west-2.
- Acceptance tests: confirm data never leaves primary region during steady state; confirm cross-region failover only on simulated outage and that failback retains integrity.
- RTO/RPO targets: propose RTO=15m for intra-region failover, RTO=2h for cross-region failover; RPO=5m for both.
- Security docs: include SOC2 PDF, KMS integration notes, and network/VPC peering options for Private deployments.
- Procurement: draft contract language limiting cross-region backups to opt-in and specifying backup retention controls.

Marissa — can you review the acceptance criteria and confirm feasibility? Aditya — once we have Marissa's sign-off, I'll send this MAP to John and his procurement team and propose dates for a 2-week POC.

Thanks,
